title: Normalize all sh-bound paths to forward slashes for Git-for-Windows compat
context: Git-for-Windows passes filter/hook/transport commands to sh, which eats backslashes outside quotes, breaking fixture scripts (127 errors) and preventing hooks from firing. Paths embedded in git config values and shell scripts must survive sh's backslash interpretation. Touches invariant(s): con_7217ab24ab (Regression guard: "Flaky test failure under parallelism: native tree-sitter module resolution race on Windows" must not recur.).
decision: Introduced shPath() helper to convert backslashes to forward slashes for all paths reaching sh (config values, env vars, shell script contents). Forward slashes work across all sh implementations including Git-for-Windows. Applied consistently across 6 test files and fixture setup code.
consequences: Fixture shell scripts now execute correctly on Windows, enabling hooks and filter tests
Control assertions can now verify attacks are live (previously blocked by command-not-found)
Path canonicalization moves from ad-hoc escaping to a single abstraction point (shPath)
Test cleanup requires bounded retry (cleanupDir) to handle Windows process handle lag
Sqlite WAL files committed into baseline fixtures are now prevented via .gitignore to unblock reset --hard
alternatives_rejected: Escape backslashes differently within shell strings (sh interprets them inconsistently)
Use Windows-native quoting or path styles in git config (git-for-Windows sh doesn't honor them)
Avoid sh by switching to native Windows tools (breaks git's standard filter/hook/transport abstraction)
Accept broken tests on Windows (leaves control assertions unable to verify live attacks)
Fix one call site at a time without abstraction (would leave inconsistency and maintenance burden)
